description: BullMQ - Message Queue and Batch processing for NodeJS, Python, .NET, Elixir, Rust and PHP based on Redis or PostgreSQL

summary.one_liner: BullMQ is a Redis-based (and, per its topics, PostgreSQL-capable) distributed job and message queue library for Node.js, with sibling implementations in Python, Rust, Elixir, .NET and PHP in the same ecosystem.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a Node.js/TypeScript library that lets you add jobs to named queues, process them with workers, and listen for completion or failure events through QueueEvents. FlowProducer creates parent-child job trees, where a parent can depend on its children. The feature comparison table lists capabilities such as delayed jobs, priorities, concurrency, rate limiting, repeatable jobs, pause/resume, sandboxed workers, deduplication, and batches (the batches and group features are marked as BullMQ-Pro only). The README says the repo also hosts Python, Rust, Elixir, .NET and PHP versions in subdirectories, and mentions a BullMQ Proxy for other languages. A paid web front end from Taskforce.sh is mentioned, and the README includes a Dragonfly sponsor note. The README does not give detailed usage of the non-Node implementations.
use_cases: background job processing in Node.js apps
processing messages with retries and priorities
how_to_run: If using node-redis adapter (createNodeRedisClient), install redis >= 5.0.0
If using Valkey Glide adapter (createValkeyGlideClient), install @valkey/valkey-glide
Create a Queue: new Queue('Paint') and queue.add('cars', { color: 'blue' })
Create a Worker: new Worker('Paint', async job => { ... }) to process jobs
Listen for results with new QueueEvents('Paint') and queueEvents.on('completed' | 'failed', ...)
notable: Official sibling implementations for Python, Rust, Elixir, .NET and PHP in one project family
FlowProducer for parent-child job dependency trees
Pluggable Redis clients: node-redis and Valkey Glide adapters
Dragonfly is noted as a drop-in Redis replacement compatible with BullMQ
Feature comparison table against Bull, Kue, Bee and Agenda
caveats: Some features (groups, batches, group rate limits, observables) are listed only for BullMQ-Pro, the paid edition
Full web UI is a separate paid offering from Taskforce.sh
README points to external documentation for most details
